headline_marked: Friend [[confesses to killing businessman]] over 3 lakh taka debt in Lalbagh
headline: Friend confesses to killing businessman over 3 lakh taka debt in Lalbagh
summary: Sheikh Wasim, 47, was found buried beneath a five-story building after being missing for three days. The suspect, a childhood friend, confessed to the murder in court.
details: A childhood friend has confessed in court to the murder of businessman Sheikh Wasim, also known as Roni, who was found buried beneath a building in Old Dhaka's Lalbagh area.
Police recovered the body of the 47-year-old victim from beneath a five-story building on BC Das Street. The body was found with hands and feet tied and plastic wrapped around the face.
The suspect, identified as Masum, reportedly killed Wasim after the latter pressured him to return a loan of 3 lakh taka. Masum had previously borrowed the money from Wasim about five months prior.
According to police, Masum lured Wasim to his imitation jewelry factory on Tuesday, where a physical altercation ensued. Masum then struck Wasim in the head and strangled him to death.
To hide the crime, the suspect tied the victim's and buried him in the ground, covering the spot with sand and cement.

The victim's brother had filed a General Diary (GD) after Wasim went missing on Tuesday. Masum was present at the police station during the filing of the GD, but was later arrested following a mobile phone tracking investigation.
The victim's wife, Nusrat Jahan, has filed a formal murder case. The court has sent the suspect to jail following his confessional statement.

According to police, Masum lured Wasim to his imitation jewelry factory on Tuesday, where a physical altercation ensued. Masum then struck Wasim in the head and strangled him to death.

To hide the crime, the suspect tied the victim's and buried him in the ground, covering the spot with sand and cement.

The victim's brother had filed a General Diary (GD) after Wasim went missing on Tuesday. Masum was present at the police station during the filing of the GD, but was later arrested following a mobile phone tracking investigation.

headline_marked: [[Journalist found dead]] at Samakal Barishal office, five notes recovered
headline: Journalist found dead at Samakal Barishal office, five notes recovered
summary: Pulak Chatterjee, a former bureau chief and Press Club general secretary, left behind notes citing distress over illness and unemployment.
details: Journalist Pulak Chatterjee was found dead at the Barishal bureau office of the Bangla daily Samakal on Friday.
Police recovered five notes from the scene, leading them to believe the death was a suicide. The notes detailed his distress over prolonged illness and unemployment.
In one note, Pulak mentioned that he had sought treatment in Vellore, India, but his condition did not improve, stating he could no longer bear the suffering.
A heartbreaking note addressed to his daughter, Prakritee, asked for forgiveness and urged her to continue her studies and music lessons while staying with her uncle.
Pulak was a prominent figure in the local media community, having served as the former bureau chief of Samakal and general secretary of the Barishal Press Club.
His body was taken to Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital for an autopsy, despite a request in one of the notes to forgo the procedure.
caption:
